newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Friday due to sharp losses on the domestic A share markets on both the Shanghai and Shenzhen bourses, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract fell to 11.70 percent from 14.50 percent on Thursday.
Turnover shrank to 7.92 million lots from 14.63 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"Some big institutions pulled out of the plunging markets today and deposited funds on the repo market, depressing the repo rates," said one trader.
Shanghai's A share index plunged 4.80 percent and its Shenzhen counterpart lost 4.33 percent on Friday after Beijing said it would crack down on manipulators on the stock marekts.
Traders expect the repo rates to recover early next week due to a few new domestic A share listings.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on Friday, with liquidity flowing back from the falling A share markets, traders said.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006, a market barometer, closed little changed at 122.94 yuan from 122.95, indicating sentiment was little changed, they said.
"The 10-year one opened higher but closed lower with heavy selling from big institutions," one trader said.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market fell sharply to 739,159 lots from 2.15 million.
Traders expect the rates to consolidate at current levels next week.
